subject: Post-call: Pilot success criteria & eval split (offline vs shadow)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@cygnushealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Pilot success criteria & eval split (offline vs shadow)

Marcus — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the trial environment.

Call recap (30m):
- Use case: clinical triage assistant for inbound patient queries (symptom intake + routing).
- Key constraints: PII handling, sub-2s median response for routing decisions, throughput ~80 qps peak for 1 clinic.
- Evaluation ask: Cygnus needs measurable success gates for go/no-go after 3-week pilot.

Proposed pilot structure (high level):
1) Week 0: Data ingestion and scope — send 2k de-identified sample chat logs + current routing rules.
2) Week 1: Offline evals (batch) — holdout set, precision/recall on routing labels, fidelity checks.
3) Week 2: Online shadow (non-canonical responses) — live traffic shadowing behind current router to measure latency, safety filtering effectiveness.
4) Week 3: Acceptance & go/no-go — run evaluation rubric and review runbook.

Success criteria (draft):
- Routing accuracy >= 88% on holdout (offline).
- No PII leakage incidents in synthetic + de-id checks.
- 95th percentile latency (shadow path) <= 2s.
- Operator false positive rate for escalations <= 7%.

Next steps (please confirm):
- Marcus: share the de-identified sample logs and the current routing taxonomy by EOD Mon (28 Jun).
- Cygnus procurement: confirm PO window and any required redlines for pilot data access.
- Rishi: prepping an initial grading rubric and checklist (attached draft).
- Lauren: set up kickoff docs and success review meeting for week 3.

I've attached a starter POC checklist and a one-page rubric. Happy to tighten numbers if you have internal targets — thought I'd propose what we discussed.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx, cygnus-grading-rubric-v1.md

From: Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@cygnushealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cygnushealth.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 18:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pilot success criteria & eval split (offline vs shadow)

Thanks Olga — that layout looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data: We'll deliver ~2.1k de-identified inbound chats by Tue (28 Jun). Will include a mapping file for your routing taxonomy.
2) Acceptance targets: the 88% routing accuracy is our baseline. Ideally we'd like to see >=92% but understand pilot constraints.
3) Shadow: we can run shadow on 10% of live traffic during Week 2. Can Redwood guarantee the shadow path will not add latency to the canonical path? (We need proof it’s non-intrusive.)

Procurement has looped in our security review; they may ask for the SOC2 evidence you referenced. I assume Rishi will coordinate the technical evidence.

I can confirm PO for the pilot budget next week pending a short SOW.

—Marcus
Marcus Doyle
Director of Product Operations | Cygnus Health
marcus.doyle@cygnushealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0440

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@cygnushealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pilot success criteria & eval split (offline vs shadow)

Marcus — appreciate the quick confirmation. Short answers then an attached rubric note.

Shadow latency: yes — shadowing is strictly asynchronous on our side (we fork a copy of the request post-routing) and we instrument with sampling to prove zero-impact on the canonical path. We'll provide a latency whitebox for the first 48 hours of shadow run.

SOC2 & security evidence: attaching the standard SOC2 summary + our network isolation checklist. I'll also add the specific KMS/HSM details for the private keying used for dataset uploads in the pilot.

Grading rubric highlights (summary):
- Offline (holdout) metrics: precision/recall per routing class, macro F1, distribution shift flags (population buckets). Pass if macro F1 >= 0.88 and no class has F1 < 0.70.
- Shadow metrics: end-to-end latency distribution (median, p95), safety filter false-positive and false-negative rates, operator override frequency. Pass if p95 <= 2s and operator override <= 7% for two consecutive days.
- Risk gates: any detected PII or safety model regression triggers immediate halt; we will conduct a joint investigation within 24h.

Ask for Cygnus: please indicate which routing classes are critical (tier A/B/C) so we can weight the rubric accordingly. Also confirm whether we can run a small synthetic PII-injection test as part of the holdout evaluation (we can show automated detection).

I'm attaching the detailed rubric document and the small SOC summary. Olga — happy to walk Marcus through the rubric tomorrow if that helps.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: cygnus-grading-rubric-v1.md, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

- Mark routing classes: Triage (A), Urgent Escalation (A), Scheduling (B), Billing/Insurance (C).
- Confirm we’re OK with the synthetic PII injection test (please keep it controlled).
- Send de-identified dataset + taxonomy by EOD today (28 Jun).

Procurement: noted — I'll push for the PO and get you any additional compliance questions they file.

Olga/Rishi — can you confirm kickoff for Mon Jul 5 (Week 0 start) and a final review on Fri Jul 23 (end of Week 3) ?

Best,
Marcus
